quote: inner += vline(100, 50) + vline(400, 50) + vline(200, 99) + vline(175, 1); … <text class="cl a" x="${xs(215)}" y="${py(99) - 4}" text-anchor="start">ED99</text><text class="cl b" x="${xs(168)}" y="${py(1) - 8}" text-anchor="end">LD1</text>
source: The curves are drawn with cum(ed, 4), whose 99% point is at ed·99^¼ ≈ 315 µg/kg and 1% point at 400/99^¼ ≈ 127 µg/kg, so the dashed ED99 line at 200 meets the effect curve at ~94% and the LD1 line at 175 meets the death curve at ~3%; the labels float off the curves. His poll figure (pollev-quantal-ti) has ED99 ≈ 210 and LD1 ≈ 175 because its curves are steeper.
fix: Use a steeper slope so the marks land on the curves: cum(100, 7) and cum(400, 7) give ED99 ≈ 193 and LD1 ≈ 207 (then LD1 ≈ ED99, as on his figure); or compute the marks from the drawn curves (ED99 = 100·99^(1/n), LD1 = 400/99^(1/n)).

quote: if (ANIM_TIMER) { clearInterval(ANIM_TIMER); ANIM_TIMER = null; b.textContent = 'Play'; return; }
source: With two step-throughs on one page (every .pair on Tell apart / Guides), pressing Play on the second figure stops the first figure's timer but resets the label of the button that was pressed, so the first figure's button keeps reading 'Pause' while nothing plays; pressing it again starts playing with the label still 'Pause'. Manual Back/Next during Play are also overridden by the timer's private index i.
fix: Keep the timer per figure: let ANIM = null; … if (ANIM) { clearInterval(ANIM.t); ANIM.b.textContent = 'Play'; const same = ANIM.b === b; ANIM = null; if (same) return; } ANIM = {t: setInterval(…), b}; and inside the interval read the current step from the DOM (steps.findIndex(s => s.classList.contains('on'))) instead of a captured i.

quote: Receptor: untouched; the second messenger it makes is broken down more slowly, so more of it accumulates.
